author_claim: In Romans 4:3, the Greek term ἐλογίσθη employs a financial accounting metaphor meaning 'was set down on the credit side.'
short_quote: metaphor from accounts, 'was set down,' here 'on the credit side.'
source_locator: Commentary on Rom 4:3, p. 100 (PDF slice p. 12)
qualification: Sanday & Headlam note legal usage in LXX for imputation of guilt (Lev 7:8, 17:4). Secondary historical commentary.

author_claim: Paul maintains a stricter adherence to the text of Genesis 15:6 than James by focusing exclusively on faith rather than appealing to later narrative events like the offering of Isaac.
short_quote: We notice at once that St. Paul keeps more strictly to his text. Gen. xv. 6 speaks only of faith.
source_locator: Note on Rom 4:7-8 / Gen 15:6, p. 102 (PDF slice p. 14)
qualification: Authors note James supports works by appealing to later Gen 22 Isaac incident.

author_claim: Paul utilized an Old Greek manuscript tradition of Hosea 2:23 reflecting the reading of Codex Vaticanus (ἀγαπήσω τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην) rather than the majority Septuagint reading (ἐλεήσω τὴν οὐκ ἠλεημένην).
short_quote: In the second clause St. Paul seems to have used a text containing the reading of the Vatican MS., for the latter can hardly have been altered to harmonize with him.
source_locator: Commentary on Rom 9:25-26, p. 264 (PDF slice p. 15)
qualification: Codex Vaticanus preserves ἀγαπήσω against majority LXX and 1 Pet 2:10 (ἐλεηθέντες). Secondary commentary claim on textual transmission.

author_claim: Paul inverted the clause order of Hosea 2:23 and substituted καλέσω for ἐρῶ under the verbal influence of ἐκάλεσεν in Romans 9:24 to emphasize the divine calling of the Gentiles.
short_quote: St. Paul inverts the order of the clauses ... and for ἐρῶ substitutes καλέσω which naturally crept in from the ἐκάλεσεν of the previous verse
source_locator: Commentary on Rom 9:25, p. 264 (PDF slice p. 15)
qualification: καλέσω with double accusative means 'I will name'; verbal catchword assimilation from Rom 9:24.

author_claim: The primary textual divergence between Paul's quotation of Hosea 1:10 in Romans 9:26 and the Septuagint is Paul's insertion of ἐκεῖ to stress the locus of divine reception.
short_quote: The only difference between St. Paul's quotation and the LXX is that he inserts ἐκεῖ :this insertion seems to emphasize the idea of the place
source_locator: Commentary on Rom 9:26, p. 264 (PDF slice p. 15)
qualification: Authors present two alternative interpretations of 'place': Palestine/Jerusalem vs universal earth.

author_claim: Paul adds the universal quantifier πᾶς ('everyone') to his quotation of Isaiah 28:16 in Romans 10:11 to prove that faith in Christ is the universal condition of salvation for Jews and Gentiles alike.
short_quote: Quoted from Is. xxviii. 16 (see above, ix. 33) with the addition of πᾶς to bring out the point on which emphasis is to be laid.
source_locator: Commentary on Rom 10:11, p. 290 (PDF slice p. 23)
qualification: Connects back to Rom 9:33 where πᾶς was absent.

author_claim: Paul quotes Joel 2:32 verbatim in Romans 10:13 to clinch his argument, applying the divine Old Testament name Κύριος directly to Jesus Christ.
short_quote: the quotation agrees with both the LXX and the Hebrew texts ... The term Κύριος is applied to Christ by St. Paul in this connection.
source_locator: Commentary on Rom 10:13, p. 291 (PDF slice p. 24)
qualification: Original text refers to Jehovah in day of the Lord; applied christologically to Christian salvation.

author_claim: Paul cites Isaiah 40:13 in Romans 11:34 with only slight variation from the Septuagint to confirm the unsearchable depth of God's wisdom and judgments.
short_quote: This is taken from Is. xl. 13, varying only very slightly from the LXX. It is quoted also 1 Cor. ii. 16.
source_locator: Commentary on Rom 11:34, p. 340 (PDF slice p. 31)
qualification: Contrasted with v. 35 (Job 41:11) which varies considerably from LXX.

author_claim: Paul's citation of Isaiah 11:10 in Romans 15:12 adopts the Septuagint's paraphrastic rendering to describe the Messianic reign of the 'root of Jesse' over the Gentiles.
short_quote: The quotation follows the LXX, which is only a paraphrase of the Hebrew
source_locator: Commentary on Rom 15:12, p. 399 (PDF slice p. 35)
qualification: Compares LXX ὁ ἀνιστάμενος ἄρχειν ἐθνῶν with Hebrew MT ('which standeth for an ensign').
